clue.text: Uproar follows a little butter for loyal one

indicators.note: the uproar comes after the butter, so its letters are placed second

parts.note: a pat is a small portion of butter
an uproar is a riot

explanation.surface: A row breaks out after someone takes a small piece of butter, and a faithful companion is involved.
explanation.definitionFit: A patriot is someone devoted and faithful to their country, a loyal citizen.

clue.text: Split hairs!

parts.note: not quibbling but literally dividing the hair on the head into two sides with a comb

explanation.definitionFit: The line combed through the hair, dividing it into two sides, is called this.

clue.text: He wants to help the enemy state his attitude

definitions.text: He wants to help the enemy state his attitude

parts.words: He wants to help the enemy state his attitude
parts.note: someone whose stated attitude is support for the enemy is a betrayer of their own side

explanation.surface: A man explains his attitude toward the enemy.
explanation.definitionFit: A betrayer who aids the enemy against their own country is the classic turncoat.

clue.text: People who are boiling sweets just right for them!

definitions.text: People who are boiling sweets just right for them!

parts.words: People who are boiling sweets just right for them
parts.note: on a sweltering day, hot people find frozen desserts exactly what they need; boiling sweets is a red herring for hard candy

explanation.surface: A confectioner's note about who makes boiled sweets.
explanation.definitionFit: Frozen dairy desserts are the treats that suit overheated people on a hot day.

clue.text: Drapes them along the edge of it, frequently

definitions.text: Drapes them along the edge of it, frequently

parts.words: Drapes them along the edge of it, frequently
parts.note: curtains or drapes often have decorative hanging tufts of thread along their hems

explanation.surface: Instructions for hanging something along an edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornamental tufts of loose threads are often sewn along the hems of curtains.

clue.text: Get bigger? Swell!

definitions.meaning: to puff up or bloat from pressure inside

explanation.definitionFit: To distend is to expand outward from internal pressure, both enlarging and bloating.

clue.text: They'll get round to you if you're patient

definitions.text: They'll get round to you if you're patient

parts.words: They'll get round to you if you're patient
parts.note: patient means a person under medical care, not someone willing to wait; physicians do rounds of their patients

explanation.surface: Reassurance that someone will deal with you eventually if you wait calmly.
explanation.definitionFit: Physicians make rounds of the wards, visiting each person under their care.

clue.text: Suggests indifference to this movement

parts.note: reads like apathy toward a political movement, but the movement is a raising of the shoulders that signals not caring

explanation.surface: Someone shows no interest in a political cause.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifting the shoulders briefly is the gesture that signals not caring or not knowing.

clue.text: Time to go back and dry the grass that's put out.

indicators.note: the word time is told to go back, so its letters are read in reverse

parts.note: to ted is to spread out mown grass so it dries into hay

explanation.surface: A farmer explains when to return and turn the hay that's been laid out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go back' turns TIME into EMIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something emitted has been given off or sent out, as smoke or sound.

clue.text: Mightily feared dead Red (that's misspelt)…

indicators.note: a word spelt wrongly has its letters jumbled, so these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone writes a note about a dead communist and admits a spelling slip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misspelt' rearranges DEAD RED into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dreaded is regarded with great fear or apprehension.

clue.text: Their pupils receive information from books

definitions.text: Their pupils receive information from books

parts.words: Their pupils receive information from books
parts.note: pupils are the eyes of those who read, taking in knowledge from printed pages rather than schoolchildren

explanation.surface: Teachers' students learn facts from textbooks.
explanation.definitionFit: People who read have eyes, or pupils, that take in knowledge from printed pages.

clue.text: A rifle short!

parts.note: sounds like being one gun too few, but describes a firearm with a short barrel

explanation.surface: Someone is missing a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A short-barrelled rifle, originally carried by cavalry, is this kind of firearm.

clue.text: Drop down dead, It were

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Drop down dead, It were': a word appears to be missing (likely 'as it were'), and no source gives the full clue

clue.text: Ten gaoled wild characters did a stretch

indicators.note: wild characters are letters running out of control, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ten unruly prisoners served a prison sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'did a stretch' hints at prison time, but it means lengthened; 'wild' rearranges TEN GAOLED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something elongated has been lengthened or drawn out, as if stretched.

clue.text: Old enemies of the Common market

definitions.text: Old enemies of the Common market

parts.words: Old enemies of the Common market
parts.note: former wartime foes of Britain who were by then members of the European Economic Community, called the Common Market

explanation.surface: Historic foes of the European trading bloc.
explanation.walkthrough: The Common Market was the British name for the European Economic Community; West Germany was a founder member, though Britain had fought it in two world wars.
explanation.definitionFit: The people of a founding Common Market country were Britain's foes in both world wars.

clue.text: Wheels held fast car that travelled like this

definitions.text: Wheels held fast car that travelled like this

parts.words: Wheels held fast car that travelled like this
parts.note: braked wheels locked while a speeding car carried on slithering along the road

explanation.surface: A fast car's wheels were gripped as it travelled.
explanation.definitionFit: A car whose locked wheels slide over the road without turning has slithered this way.

clue.text: Not knowing what it's called

parts.note: reads as forgetting a name, but the phrase also names the state of not knowing itself

explanation.surface: Someone cannot remember the name of a thing.
explanation.definitionFit: The state of lacking knowledge is exactly what not knowing is called.

clue.text: Before the judge, such a one turns up to take charge

definitions.text: Before the judge, such a one turns up to take charge

parts.words: Before the judge, such a one turns up to take charge
parts.note: the defendant appears in court to face a charge, not to take command

explanation.surface: Someone arrives in court to take control of proceedings.
explanation.definitionFit: A defendant standing in court facing a criminal charge is the person so described.

clue.text: Made one from a list of separate figures

definitions.text: Made one from a list of separate figures

parts.words: Made one from a list of separate figures
parts.note: a column of numbers totalled into a single sum

explanation.surface: Someone created a person from a list of separate characters.
explanation.definitionFit: Totalled a column of numbers into one sum, the arithmetic sense of the phrase.

clue.text: Hard cash!

parts.note: money in physical metal form, literally hard, rather than ready money in general

explanation.definitionFit: Metal money minted as coins is literally hard currency.

clue.text: Situation caused by sharp fall of rain, might one say?

definitions.text: Situation caused by sharp fall of rain, might one say?

parts.words: Situation caused by sharp fall of rain, might one say
parts.note: a sharp fall in rainfall, meaning a steep drop in its amount, rather than a heavy shower

explanation.surface: A sudden downpour causes problems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sharp fall of rain' suggests a cloudburst, but the fall is a decline in the amount of rain.
explanation.definitionFit: A long spell with too little rain, a steep fall in rainfall, is this dry condition.

clue.text: They frighten fellows with cards

parts.note: fellows are men
aces are high playing cards

explanation.surface: Card sharps intimidate their opponents at the table.
explanation.definitionFit: Threats or dangers that frighten people are menaces.

clue.text: Went into business without the consent of the partners!

definitions.text: Went into business without the consent of the partners!

parts.words: Went into business without the consent of the partners
parts.note: not starting a firm but poking into other people's affairs uninvited

explanation.surface: Someone set up a company without their partners' approval.
explanation.definitionFit: Interfered in matters that were none of one's business, uninvited by those involved.

clue.text: Is able to write "Farewell to a Child" as a piece of music

parts.note: is able means can
ta-ta is the goodbye said to or by a small child

explanation.surface: A composer can write a work called Farewell to a Child.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantata is a vocal composition with soloists and chorus, a musical work.

clue.text: Stop one working for a while, and splash out in America

definitions.text: Stop one working for a while

indicators.note: America is placed in the splashing out, splitting it after its first letter

parts.note: to splash out is to spend lavishly
US is the abbreviation for the United States

explanation.surface: Someone is laid off temporarily and goes on a spending spree in the States.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspend a worker is to stop them working temporarily, often as discipline.

clue.text: Waterlogs it, maybe!

parts.note: waterlogs read as water logs: logs floating on the water, as an example

explanation.surface: Something becomes soaked through.
explanation.definitionFit: Timber washed up or floating at sea is literally logs on the water.

clue.text: Junk food:!

definitions.meaning: the stomach lining of cattle, eaten as a dish

explanation.definitionFit: Tripe is both worthless rubbish and cow's stomach cooked as a dish.

clue.text: Payments demanded by letter

parts.note: a letter here is one who lets property, a landlord, not a written message

explanation.surface: Bills requested through the post.
explanation.definitionFit: Periodic sums paid to a landlord for property are what a landlord collects.

clue.text: Picture-house room

definitions.meaning: a sketch made with pencil or pen
a ... room is a formal sitting room in a house

explanation.definitionFit: A sketch is a picture, and a drawing room is a formal room in a house.

clue.text: Passed on one's ancestry

parts.note: a line of descent handed down through the generations

explanation.surface: Someone transmitted their heritage to descendants.
explanation.definitionFit: One's line of descent from forebears is one's ancestry, handed down generation by generation.

clue.text: One learning to be in a position of authority

definitions.text: One learning to be in a position of authority

parts.words: One learning to be in a position of authority
parts.note: a senior pupil, still learning at school, who is given authority over younger ones

explanation.surface: A trainee manager learning to take charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior school pupil given disciplinary authority over others while still a student.

clue.text: Five hundred hired a new sort of Tory

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500

indicators.note: new signals the letters of the two words are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A party hires five hundred people to form a new kind of Conservative.
explanation.walkthrough: A Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party; 'a new sort of' reads as part of the definition, but 'new' is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A die-hard is an unyielding traditionalist, the most stubbornly conservative kind of party member.
